entries.title: Isaiah 17:2
segments: They shall be for flocks; desolated and converted into common pasture-ground.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:3
segments: Ephraim is joined with Damascus in this prophecy, because the two kingdoms were confederate against Judah.
They shall be as the glory of the children of Israel; their glory shall be brought low, like that of the children of Israel.
They who are united in persecuting God's people, must also be in the destruction which he brings upon their enemies.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:5
segments:
It shall be; with Israel and his glory. 
 
  As when the harvest-man--he that gathereth ears; his enenmies shall reap him as one reaps grain. 
 
  In the valley of Rephaim; a plain near Jerusalem on the south-west. It is probably mentioned here because of its luxuriant fields of grain. 
 
vv 5-6. 
 
The mightiest among God's enemies are utterly feeble and helpless in his hands.  They fall before his wrath like the ears of corn before the reaper, and like oliveberries before the gatherer.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:6
segments:
Gleaning grapes; literally, gleanings; here, gleanings of olive-berrries. 
 
  Shall be left in it--in the outmost fruitful branches; a remnant only of Israel shall be left, like the scattered berries on the topmost boughs of an olive-tree after the fruit has been gathered.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:7
segments:
Look to his Maker; in faith and obedience, the fruit of the chastisement inflicted by God on his people. 
 
vv 7-8. 
 
God's chastisements are adapted and designed to withdraw the confidence of his people from the vain objects in which worldly men put their trust; and in respect to the "remnant according to the election of grace," they always accomplish this result.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:8
segments: Groves; or, "images of Ashtoreth," a female goddess worshipped by the Zidonians and other heathen nations.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:9
segments: A forsaken bough; or, " the remnant of a forest."

An uppermost branch; on which a few berries are left. 
 
  Because of the children of Israel; or, "As the ruins in forests and on hills which they," the Canaanites, "left," in fleeing "before the face of the children of Israel."

entries.title: Isaiah 17:10
segments: Pleasant plants--strange slips; a figurative description of idolatrous practices, as arising from forgetfulness of God.  "Strange slips," are slips from "a strange vine."

vv 10-11. 
 
They who forget the living God, and seek prosperity and salvation from their own worldly devices, reap in the end a harvest of "grief and of desperate sorrow."

entries.title: Isaiah 17:11
segments: A heap; a ruinous heap; that is, their idolatrous observances shall bring to them "grief and desperate sorrow."

entries.title: Isaiah 17:12
segments:
The multitude of many people; gathered against Zion.  From the confederacy of Syria and Ephraim the prophet passes to a general denunciation of God's wrath upon the persecutors of his people. 
 
vv 12-14. 
 
Since God dwells among his people, they have no reason to fear the power of their foes, however formidable it may seem.  He can destroy in a moment all thier combined hosts, as stubble is blown before the whirlwind.

entries.title: Isaiah 17:14
segments:
Trouble; consternation falling upon the host of Zion's enemies. 
 
  He is not; he has perished.  This prophecy was strikingly fulfilled upon Sennacherib's army, but should not be restricted to that overthrow.
